quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended and red lights flashing, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Keep driving when you think most children have left the bus.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely when a school bus has stopped with its stop arm extended and red lights flashing. Stay stopped until the stop arm is pulled back in and the lights stop flashing.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or slope.
When parked on a flat road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or slope.
questions.explanation: When parked uphill or downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or edge. This prevents your car from rolling into traffic if your brakes fail. At traffic lights, keep wheels straight so a rear-end collision won't push you into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: As your speed increases, you should:

options.text: Look far ahead on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. When driving fast, look far ahead so you have time to react safely to hazards.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not count on the other driver giving you space to return to your lane.
Assume the driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not count on the other driver giving you space to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even with a signal, do not assume other drivers will give you space or let you pass. Never count on it.

questions.question: When bright headlights shine toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other car passes.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look at the right edge of the road until the other car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: Before entering an intersection, look to your:
questions.explanation: Look left, then right, then left again before entering. Vehicles from your left will be closer than vehicles from your right. Check that the path through the intersection is clear.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign means:
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of special conditions or hazards ahead. They are usually yellow or orange with black text.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, drive at:

options.text: The same speed as freeway traffic.
A slower speed than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter a freeway at the same speed as traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should drive slowly and turn on your:
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever visibility is poor. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended for driving with a blood alcohol level of:
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol if you are under 21. Any trace of alcohol will result in license suspension for two years and other penalties.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not brake during a skid. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: Do not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: If you are already in an intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Continue and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are in the intersection when it turns yellow, drive through quickly and safely to clear it.

questions.question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, you should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.

questions.explanation: Follow a police officer's directions. They override traffic lights and signs.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to areas where bicycles and other traffic may cross.

questions.question: Construction zone signs are usually:

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red colors.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow colors.
Diamond or rectangular with orange and black colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond or rectangular with orange and black colors.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange with black letters or symbols. They appear on the right side of the road, or on both sides on divided highways.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter medicines are safe if taken as directed.
Prescription medications are always safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications, prescription or over-the-counter, can impair your driving. Cold and allergy medicines often cause drowsiness. Know how your medications affect you before driving.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors them.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything possible to prevent hitting a pedestrian, no matter the circumstances.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This warning sign alerts you to a fork in the road. You must choose to go right or left.

questions.question: Use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is in your way.

questions.explanation: Use your horn only when it helps prevent a collision. Do not use it to tell drivers to go faster or move out of your way.

questions.question: To make room for cars entering the freeway, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.explanation: Move to another lane to make space for cars entering the freeway. If you cannot move lanes, slow down to let them enter safely.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. You should:

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic when you can.
Speed up to protect your right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic when you can.
questions.explanation: When possible, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane safely.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: No one can pass from either direction.
Everyone can pass from either direction.
Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only drivers next to the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: Drivers next to the dashed line can pass. Drivers next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Press hard on the gas pedal.

questions.explanation: Put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Mirrors cannot show what is directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: You must use low beam headlights when driving:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and create glare. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: A dashed white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Lanes go in opposite directions and drivers cannot pass.
Lanes go in the same direction and drivers cannot pass.
Lanes go in the same direction and drivers can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes go in the same direction and drivers can pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. Dashed lines mean you can pass when it is safe.

questions.question: You park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels so the vehicle rolls away from the road center if your brakes fail.

questions.question: Sudden wind gusts on highways:
questions.explanation: Wind affects all drivers. It can reduce visibility and physically move your vehicle.

questions.question: You see animals standing near the road. You should:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Quickly switch to the next lane.

questions.explanation: Animals may run into the road suddenly. They may also travel in groups, so more may be hidden from view.

questions.question: Slowing down to look at crashes or unusual events:
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at crashes or unusual events. This causes traffic jams.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Use high beams until you are 10 feet away.

questions.explanation: Use low beams when following another car. Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are near.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Expect workers to yield to you.

questions.explanation: Drive with extra care in construction zones. Conditions can change suddenly, and you need to protect yourself, other drivers, and workers.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than regular cars.

questions.question: After a crash, you must give your name, address, and vehicle information:

options.text: Every time you are in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you are in a crash.
questions.explanation: You must stop after every crash and share your license, name, address, and vehicle information with other drivers involved.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and a siren while you are in an intersection. You should:

options.text: Stop right away in the intersection.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing, then pull right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing, then pull right and stop.
questions.explanation: Continue through the intersection, then move to the right and stop. You must yield to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days so:

options.text: Other drivers can see your vehicle.
You can warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, headlights help other drivers see you. If you need windshield wipers, turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. To prevent it in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep steady speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.explanation: Slow down in rain. Driving too fast can make your tires lose contact with the road, making it hard to control your vehicle.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, check:
questions.explanation: By definition, mirrors cannot show blind spots. Look over your shoulders to check blind spots.

questions.question: Your vehicle breaks down, you should:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic. Turn on your emergency flashers so other drivers see you are disabled.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid line.
Allowed from the side with the broken line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken line.
questions.explanation: Passing is allowed from the side next to the broken line and not allowed from the side next to the solid line.
